items.title: Dynamics of emotion-transition networks link brain network variability and affective symptoms
items.author: Yu Li
items.content: This study investigates the dynamic organization and temporal transitions of daily emotional states and examines their neural correlates using brain imaging data. It shows that reduced tendency to maintain or return to low negative affect is associated with depressive and anxiety symptoms and may involve temporal variability in the salience network.

items.title: Fatigue and processing speed predict subsequent fatigue override, evidence from a coordinated analysis of six EMA studies
items.author: Raeanne C. Moore
items.content: This study analyzes six intensive longitudinal studies with 1,088 participants to test whether fatigue and processing speed predict people’s ability to override fatigue in daily life. Greater-than-usual fatigue and unusually fast processing speed both predict reduced fatigue override in the following hours, and clinical samples show lower override capacity.

items.title: Emergent blink rate in early childhood is associated with neural origins of executive function
items.author: Yusuke Moriguchi
items.content: Spontaneous eye-blink rate, prefrontal haemodynamic responses and cognitive flexibility are measured in 113 children aged 35–80 months. With age, prefrontal activation shifts towards a right-dorsal pattern and performance improves; a higher blink rate accompanies both, marking it as a candidate indicator of executive function development.

items.title: Educating minds with generative AI
items.author: Thomas Wachter
items.content: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly entering education, framed as a tool for efficiency and personalization. This Perspective argues that this framing of GenAI obscures a deeper transformation.

items.title: Reinforcement-trained recurrent networks reproduce human beat-synchronization dynamics
items.author: Jonathan Cannon
items.content: We train a recurrent neural network to synchronize its output with a metronome across a range of tempos using reinforcement learning. The most effective reinforcement scheme also reproduces key features of human synchronization behavior.
